levels.title: Top Chef Quickfire
levels.description: Creativity under the clock — one hero ingredient, no recipe, pure instinct.

modules.title: Pantry Raid Challenge
modules.summary: Build a composed bite from mystery basket staples in 20 minutes.
modules.practice_query: quickfire appetizer from eggs onion and citrus
teaching: Pick one technique and one flavor arc — do not attempt a full restaurant dish.
Taste twice before plating; acid fixes flat quickfire plates.
Leave 2 minutes for garnish and wipe the rim — presentation counts.

modules.title: One-Pot Speed Cook
modules.summary: Single vessel, layered flavor, served hot — no backup burner.
modules.practice_query: one-pot spiced rice and chicken under time pressure
teaching: Bloom spices in the pot first — even one-pot dishes need a flavor base.
Back-time: protein in at minute 8, garnish at minute 18.
Judges eat temperature — serve the hottest component last on the plate.

modules.title: Twist Ingredient Integration
modules.summary: Mandatory mystery ingredient must be central, not a garnish afterthought.
modules.practice_query: dish featuring assigned mystery ingredient as star
teaching: Name the ingredient on the plate — judges should taste it immediately.
Pair sweet mystery items with acid; pair earthy items with bright herbs.
If you fail the twist, nothing else saves the score.

levels.title: Hell's Kitchen Pass
levels.description: Hot line discipline — timing, communication, and perfect protein temps.

modules.title: Protein at the Pass
modules.summary: Medium-rare lamb, crispy skin chicken, rest before slice — no excuses.
modules.practice_query: two proteins to temp on a simulated dinner rush
teaching: Touch-test calibration: rare soft, medium springy, well-done firm.
Rest meat while firing garnish — use carryover to your advantage.
Call times loud: "Lamb medium, two minutes!" — silence loses services.

modules.title: Garnish & Sauce Station
modules.summary: Emulsion held, sauce napped, garnish identical on every cover.
modules.practice_query: hollandaise and reduced sauce for four identical plates
teaching: Hold sauces in bain-marie, not direct flame — broken sauce fails the pass.
Nap with ladle back-and-forth; pool sauces, do not flood the protein.
Garnish height should not block the protein — judges eat with eyes first.

modules.title: Recovery After Mistake
modules.summary: Trash it, reboot, communicate — Ramsay-level recovery drill.
modules.practice_query: recover from overseared steak with new pan sauce
teaching: Burned protein cannot be saved — re-fire or substitute before the pass.
Communicate mistake immediately; hiding it costs the whole brigade.
Fix process, not just plate — why did it burn? Adjust heat or dry surface.

levels.title: MasterChef Replication
levels.description: Recreate signature dishes from memory and written specs alone.

modules.title: Classic Dish Replication
modules.summary: Study the plate photo — sauce placement, cut size, color contrast.
modules.practice_query: replicate beef wellington style plate from reference image
teaching: Sketch the plate before cooking — quadrant map for sauce and starch.
Match cut geometry: same bias, same thickness, same count.
Color contrast matters — pale-on-pale plates read as unfinished.

modules.title: Baked Showstopper Replication
modules.summary: Structure, crumb, and decoration must mirror the reference.
modules.practice_query: replicate layered celebration cake from photo
teaching: Level cakes before stacking — replication fails on tilt.
Crumb coat hides sins; final coat shows skill.
Decoration spacing: measure with your eye using knife marks as guides.

modules.title: Blind Taste Rebuild
modules.summary: Eat once, then rebuild flavor profile without seeing the recipe.
modules.practice_query: reverse-engineer curry flavor from single tasting
teaching: Note order of sensations: sweet first bite, heat on finish, acid when?
Write spice guesses before cooking — adjust one layer at a time.
Replication is listening; ask what fat carries the spice.

levels.title: Restaurant Wars
levels.description: Concept, menu, brigade roles, and opening night service.

modules.title: Concept & Menu Design
modules.summary: Theme, price point, and a cohesive three-course arc for judges.
modules.practice_query: three-course menu with unified concept and price tier
teaching: Concept in one sentence — if you cannot, the menu wanders.
Star protein cost caps the rest of the menu; design backwards from food cost.
Amuse, intermezzo, or palate cleanser shows intention, not filler.

modules.title: Brigade Roles & Prep List
modules.summary: Assign stations, prep lists, and fire order before doors open.
modules.practice_query: prep list and station map for 20-cover pop-up service
teaching: Every item on the menu needs a owner and a par level.
Cross-train garnish and sauce — Restaurant Wars has absentees.
Fire list posted at the pass; verbal only fails under noise.

modules.title: Opening Night Service
modules.summary: Full service simulation — tickets, timing, guest complaints.
modules.practice_query: execute opening night for three-course restaurant wars menu
teaching: 86 items when quality drops — empty menu beats bad plate.
Expediter is the conductor; line cooks do not self-prioritize.
Guest complaint drill: comp, remake, or explain — decide in 30 seconds.

levels.title: Iron Chef
levels.description: Secret ingredient showdown — multiple courses, stadium energy.

modules.title: Secret Ingredient as Star
modules.summary: Three courses, one ingredient featured differently in each.
modules.practice_query: three courses starring one secret ingredient
teaching: Course 1 raw or light, course 2 main technique, course 3 comfort or dessert.
Transform texture across courses — crispy, silky, chewy.
Judges eat volume; portion small, flavor loud.

modules.title: Battle Clock Strategy
modules.summary: 60-minute war: when to start long cooks vs. fresh finishes.
modules.practice_query: iron chef timed battle with secret ingredient and rice component
teaching: Minute 0: start roast or braise; minute 30: sauces; minute 50: garnish only.
Two burners active max — plan cold dishes for relief.
Taste at minute 45; only salt and acid fixes left after.

modules.title: Stadium Plate Drama
modules.summary: Height, color, and story — plates read from the judges' balcony.
modules.practice_query: visually dramatic iron chef plate with height and color
teaching: Vertical builds read on camera — anchor with starch or ring mold.
Contrast colors: secret ingredient color dictates garnish opposite wheel.
Wipe every fingerprint; stadium lights show every smear.

levels.title: GBBO Technical
levels.description: Sparse instructions, judge standards, and bake until done — not until timer.

modules.title: Technical Sponge
modules.summary: Ingredients listed, method vague — rely on bake knowledge.
teaching: Cream butter and sugar until pale — GBBO sponges fail on under-creaming.
Eggs room temp; fold gently to keep volume.
Springs back when pressed — timer is a hint, not law.
show_refs: The Great British Bake Off — Technical Challenge

modules.title: Technical Laminated Pastry
modules.summary: Butter block integration without explicit fold count on the sheet.
teaching: Butter same consistency as dough — GBBO technicals punish warm kitchens.
Visible layers before bake; if none, folds failed.
Even golden bake — dark tips mean uneven oven or proof.
show_refs: The Great British Bake Off — Technical Challenge

modules.title: Technical Bread Shape
modules.summary: Scoring, proof, and classic shape from Paul Hollywood standards.
modules.practice_query: cob loaf or braided technical bread from brief instructions
teaching: Tight initial shape creates oven spring — slack dough spreads.
Score decisively; timid cuts burst unevenly.
Hollow tap bottom — technical bread is about sound and crumb.
show_refs: The Great British Bake Off — Technical Challenge

shows_referenced: The Great British Bake Off — Technical Challenge
